message:
feat(keepalive-r2 ②, a/b): the client side of a standby entry -- a pure state machine and a durable generation counter

Contract docs/keepalive_host_standby_contract.md §2.2/§2.6/§2.7/§3, Codex r4 '② GO'. No socket, no clock: the
caller owns the lease's one UDP socket and feeds packets and time in.
- StandbyEntryClient: Idle -> Admitting -> Parked (Ping 5 s) -> Activating -> Active -> (session end) Parked;
  Waiting (Busy / Superseded / Lost, backoff 1..30 s, then a NEW capability), Unsupported (no answer to 6 Hellos:
  an older host -- no automatic connect, never a legacy Hello).
- an activation completes only on ITS Pong (entry + generation, Granted) and the HelloAck, either order; a lost
  answer repeats Activate with the SAME generation; a bare / late / cancelled / foreign answer adopts nothing; a
  cancel sends no Release (a granted entry refuses it) -- the next activation takes a larger generation.
- a lease whose Pings go unanswered 16 s (< the 20 s lease: e.g. the relay lost the host's proof) is Lost, never
  kept as ready; an entry the host forgot (Unknown) is Lost too.
- GenerationAllocator: one monotone counter for admissions and activations, saved BEFORE use; a restart continues
  above it; an unsaved generation is never sent; nothing usable stored -> a new device id.
Shipping: nothing calls it yet (automatic preconnect stays OFF).
Test: standby_entry_client_test 46/46; mutants bareAck / anyGen / noDead / legacy / newGenRetx / noSave /
busyAtOnce all FAIL.
